parsed.rationale: Both `WXYCApp.navigateToPreviousTheme` (line 465) and `WXYCApp.navigateToNextTheme` (line 477) live in the same file (`WXYC/iOS/WXYCApp.swift`) and package (`app:iOS`), carry no restraint markers (`is_test`, `is_mock`, `is_sample_app`, `is_codegen` all false), and share a Jaccard similarity of 0.75 — indicating their bodies differ only in the direction of navigation. Introducing a single `navigateTheme(direction:)` helper removes the duplicated logic while keeping the two public entry-point names as thin, readable wrappers if they are part of a public interface, or collapsing them entirely if they are internal.

specifics.proposed_action: Unify `WXYCApp.navigateToPreviousTheme` (line 465) and `WXYCApp.navigateToNextTheme` (line 477) in `WXYC/iOS/WXYCApp.swift` into a single parameterised helper, e.g. `navigateTheme(direction: ThemeNavigationDirection)` or `navigateTheme(offset: Int)`, where the direction/offset argument encodes the ±1 step. Both call sites become one-liners delegating to the shared helper, eliminating the near-duplicate body (Jaccard 0.75).
specifics.why_no_category_fits: The two methods are not separate types, protocols, or structs — they are a symmetric pair of methods on the same class (`WXYCApp`) in the same file. 'extract-to-common' targets cross-file/cross-package duplication; 'generic-parameterization' targets type-level generics; 'subclass-lift' requires an inheritance hierarchy. The correct fix is a direction-parameterised private helper within the same file, which is closest to 'other' since no listed category covers intra-file method consolidation via a new parameter.
